function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Used 19 of 20 decisions; the red block is still standing on the table and the gripper is closed on empty air (measured opening 0.0162 after three separate close attempts at table level). With two decisions left I cannot complete grasp + lift + transport + release, so the trial cannot be finished in the remaining budget. The block was never lifted: each closure missed it in the horizontal plane because I could not calibrate the fixed cameras well enough to localise it better than roughly +/- 5 cm.", "hindsight": "Concrete facts for a future agent on this rig. (1) Motion chunks: move_to returns a step count that is essentially set by the commanded distance divided by ~28 mm, and the arm only tracks ~4-10 mm per control step, so a plain position target typically yields 1-4 steps and moves the hand only 10-40 mm, far short of the target. A large commanded GRIPPER change overrides this: gripper 0->1 or 1->0 gives a 79-80 step chunk and the arm then actually reaches its Cartesian target. Commanding an intermediate gripper value (0.4-0.5, which the adapter latches as hold-previous) is a reliable way to buy a long chunk without changing the grasp state. Plan every transport around this. (2) The reported gripper measurement is a good empty/closed discriminator: ~0.016 = closed on nothing, ~0.99 = fully open, an intermediate value would mean holding the block. (3) Geometry: table top z=0.80, the block is a ~30 mm cube, the bowl rim ~0.85. The fingertips sit roughly 50 mm BELOW the reported eef_pos, so eef z about 0.85 already puts the pads alongside a 30 mm block; do not waste calls descending further. (4) Vision: at 224x224 the fixed front and side views are nearly useless for metric servoing here - the hand moved 50-70 mm in the world for only a few pixels of image motion, so I could not settle whether each view horizontal is world x, world y or a diagonal, and my block estimates swung between (x +0.06, y -0.02) and (x -0.04, y -0.15). Best usable cue is the wrist camera, whose image right is roughly +x and image up roughly +y at ~1 mm/px near the centre, but its frame does NOT cover the volume directly under the fingertips: the block drops out of the bottom edge once the hand is within about 5 cm of it, which is easy to misread as alignment. (5) The bowl interior contains a small stationary red marker dot - do not mistake it for the red block being placed. (6) Repeated low slides with an open gripper visibly nudged the block (its front-view pixel drifted ~18 px over the trial), so approach from above and never sweep horizontally at table level. (7) Budget: 20 decisions is tight given the chunk behaviour; spend at most 3-4 on localisation, then grasp, lift, transport and release with gripper-change-driven long chunks."}
